subject: Reference rotation: advance notice & opt-out window
messages:
From: Nadia Patel <nadia@bluemed.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BlueMed Legal <legal@bluemed.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: 2–3 customer references for procurement committee

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked very promising for our workflow. Our procurement committee asked if we could speak with two to three current customers who use Redwood for high-throughput inference (ideally in healthcare analytics). They prefer references who can speak to latency SLAs, on-prem deployment, and security controls.

Ideal timeline: committee meeting on Aug 18. If possible, can you confirm availability this week for one quick intro and one deeper call next week? If any of your references need to decline, we can accept substitutes — we just need advance notice so the committee has time to reschedule.

I've attached a short RFQ and the committee's set of questions (BlueMed_ref_request.pdf).

Appreciate it — Nadia
Nadia Patel
Head of Procurement
BlueMed Analytics

Attachments: BlueMed_ref_request.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nadia Patel <nadia@bluemed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, BlueMed Legal <legal@bluemed.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 2–3 customer references for procurement committee

Hi Nadia — thanks for the RFQ and timeline. We can absolutely help — appreciate the advance notice.

Quick notes on how we handle reference requests so expectations are clear:
- We rotate references to avoid over-requesting the same contacts.
- Customers get an opt-out window (48–72 hours) to decline a request, after which we propose a substitute.
- For requests tied to procurement timelines, we prioritize scheduling but always respect customer availability and fatigue concerns.

Marissa — looping you in to suggest candidates who are reference-ready and have recent on-prem experience.

Nadia — I’ll come back with two candidate names and suggested times by EOD tomorrow (Aug 2). If the committee has a hard constraint on the Aug 18 meeting, let me know and we’ll escalate scheduling.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0134
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: 2–3 customer references for procurement committee

Jordan —

Quick candidate list (all internal ok to share):
1) Eric Thomson, GridHealth (on-prem + HIPAA) — historically responsive, OK for a 30–45m procurement call, prefers morning PST.
2) Suresh Iyer, Optima Labs — uses dedicated pools and did a recent rollout; good for cost/perf questions.
3) Maya Srinivasan, CareSight — smaller deployment but strong comments on caching and batching wins.

Recommendation: propose Eric + Suresh as primary; offer Maya as backup. I attached a draft schedule with buffer windows (reference-schedule.csv).

Also, given BlueMed's compressed timeline, I recommend we explicitly communicate a 72-hour opt-out window to each customer to avoid last-minute declines and to give them the right to postpone without pressure. Anything more aggressive (shorter window) tends to generate complaints / reference fatigue.

If accepted, I can reach out to Eric and Suresh right away. If either declines, we substitute Maya or loop in GridHealth's backup contact, Priya Shah.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: reference-schedule.csv (text/csv)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 2–3 customer references for procurement committee

Thanks for the quick coordination. Two operational guardrails from me:
1) Do not commit customers to the committee date until they explicitly accept — always give the opt-out window and suggested alternatives.
2) For procurement-driven requests, offer a one-off courtesy (e.g., a waived integration review fee or a $500 gift card) only if the reference contact is a named individual who will need to prep and join a demo. Approval for any compensation must go through legal — loop them when offering anything monetary.

If BlueMed is a strategic near-term ARR (RDW-DEAL-3491), prioritize scheduling but keep the rotation discipline — we can’t put GridHealth on the hook repeatedly. If Eric is OK and Suresh can do a shorter slot, proceed.

— Lauren
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
